key_insight: Similarity renormalization lets a trapped-ion simulator probe strongly coupled, high-occupancy static Yukawa physics despite a limited bosonic readout range.
engineering_relevance: Effective-particle representations can extend the physics accessible on qubit–boson hardware without directly expanding its measurable occupancy range.
method: Implement coupled fermion–boson dynamics on the QSCOUT trapped-ion platform.
Use similarity renormalization to describe the same physics with effective particles at different parameter values s.
Map experimentally accessible occupancy data to larger occupancies in distinct effective-particle representations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an experimental demonstration of static Yukawa time evolution on QSCOUT, but gives no quantitative accuracy or uncertainty metrics.
watch_item: The larger-occupancy results rely on renormalization-based mapping rather than direct measurement at those occupancies.
paper_title: Quantum Simulation of the Static Yukawa Model via Effective Particles on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
